payload.text:
Skill overview

Add a new purchasable skill called Scan.

Scan is a diagnostic tool that checks the current Sudoku board and reveals incorrectly placed numbers only, even if they are not obviously wrong.
It does not solve the puzzle and does not suggest correct numbers.

Skill behavior

When activated, Scan analyzes the board and detects wrong numbers:

Numbers that violate Sudoku rules in their row, column, or 3×3 box

Correct numbers must never be highlighted.

Scan does not modify the board automatically.

Usage limits & cooldown

Scan can be used maximum 3 times per game level.

Add an internal cooldown of ~2 seconds after each use to prevent double-pressing.

While cooldown is active:

The Scan button is temporarily disabled

Pressing again does nothing

Uses must NOT be consumed again

Uses indicator (IMPORTANT)

The Scan icon in the in-game toolbar must include a small circular badge showing remaining uses.

Badge behavior:

Starts at 3

Decrements on each successful Scan use:

3 → 2 → 1 → 0

When remaining uses reach 0:

Scan becomes not pressable

Scan icon is greyed out / disabled

Badge should show 0 (or be hidden if cleaner, but disabled state must be obvious)

Badge design:

Circular

Clean / minimal

Matches existing UI style

Skill selection logic (VERY IMPORTANT)

Skills are selectable tools, NOT permanent options.

Players can select multiple skills at the same time (e.g. Auto + Scan).

Only selected skills appear in the in-game toolbar.

Toolbar behavior examples:

No skills selected → Undo · Pencil · Erase

Auto selected → Undo · Pencil · Erase · Auto

Auto + Scan selected → Undo · Pencil · Erase · Auto · Scan

Toolbar buttons must re-align dynamically for clean spacing and good visualization.

Scan animation & visual feedback

When Scan is activated:

A red laser / scan line passes quickly across the entire Sudoku grid

Animation duration: ~1 second

After the scan:

Only wrong numbers are revealed

Wrong numbers receive a subtle red flashing background

This red flashing remains until the number is deleted or replaced

Replacement can be correct OR incorrect — either action clears the warning

Correct numbers must remain visually unchanged.

Economy

Skill name: Scan

Price: 750 diamonds (rhombuses)

Icon

Create an icon that clearly represents scanning / detection, not solving.

Recommended concept:

A Sudoku grid with a horizontal scan line

OR a magnifying glass over a single cell

Icon must match existing skill icons:

Minimal

Flat

Readable at small sizes

Premium look

Final notes

Scan must feel like a smart diagnostic tool, not a cheat.

Animations should be subtle and premium.

Make sure Scan works correctly alongside other skills (e.g. Auto).

Return all required UI, logic, and animation code updates needed to support this feature.

Add a new purchasable skill called Reveal.

Core behavior

When Reveal is activated, it must fill exactly ONE empty cell with the correct solution number.

The revealed cell is chosen randomly from eligible empty cells:

Cell is currently empty

Cell is not an original given

Cell is not already revealed/locked

If no eligible cells exist, Reveal should not run (disable it or show a small message like “Nothing to reveal”).

Locked (unmovable) behavior — VERY IMPORTANT

The revealed number must behave like a given:

It is not deletable

It is not replaceable/overwritable

Erase tool must not remove it

Pencil tool must not edit it

Selecting the cell should do nothing (or show a subtle “locked” feedback)

Implementation note:

Mark the cell as isRevealed: true (or isLocked: true)

Treat original givens and revealed cells as locked, but with a different visual style.

Visual style (PERMANENT)

After Reveal finishes:

The number must be black (same color as original givens)

The cell must have a permanent soft yellow background

This yellow background:

Stays visible for the rest of the level

Clearly distinguishes revealed numbers from original givens and user-entered numbers

Should be subtle, not aggressive (light yellow, premium feel)

Reveal animation (premium, NO scaling)

Total duration: ~0.8–1.0 seconds

Dim the entire grid

Subtle dark overlay (about 20–40% opacity)

Highlight the selected cell

Soft glow around the cell

Reveal the number

Correct number fades in smoothly (optionally blur → sharp)

NO scaling

Lock-in

Remove grid dim

Remove glow

Transition the cell into its permanent yellow background state

End state:

Black number

Yellow background

Locked and uneditable

Uses, ads, and persistence

Reveal has 1 use per level by default.

After use:

Remaining uses become 0

Reveal button becomes disabled / greyed out

Player can watch an ad to gain +1 additional Reveal use

Each ad grants exactly 1 Reveal use

Persistence (IMPORTANT)

Reveal usage must be saved per level:

Leaving the level

Closing/reopening the app

Refreshing

If Reveal was already used in a level, it must remain unavailable when returning.

Each level tracks Reveal uses independently.

Skill selection & toolbar logic

Reveal is a selectable skill, not a permanent option.

Players can select Reveal together with other skills (Auto, Scan).

Only selected skills appear in the in-game toolbar.

Toolbar examples:

No skills → Undo · Pencil · Erase

Auto + Scan → Undo · Pencil · Erase · Auto · Scan

Auto + Scan + Reveal → Undo · Pencil · Erase · Auto · Scan · Reveal

Toolbar must re-align dynamically for clean spacing.

Uses badge

Reveal icon shows a small circular badge with remaining uses:

Starts at 1

After use → 0

After ad → 1

When uses are 0:

Button is disabled

Icon is greyed out

Icon

Create a minimal icon representing reveal / uncover, not solve.

Suggested concepts:

Eye over a single cell

Cell with a light beam

Style must match existing icons:

Minimal

Flat

Readable at small sizes

Final notes

Reveal is a powerful but scarce relief skill.

Permanent yellow background is intentional and must be clearly visible.

Ensure compatibility with Auto and Scan.

Return all required UI, logic, persistence, and ad-handling code.

payload.text:
Add a Dark Mode setting to the app using a token-based theme system. This is a UI dark mode, not a full color inversion.

1) Settings UI

Add a new setting called Appearance

Options:

System

Light

Dark

Persist the selection (localStorage) and apply immediately.

If System is selected, follow OS preference.

2) Theme implementation (IMPORTANT)

Do NOT update colors screen-by-screen.

Implement semantic theme tokens with two themes:

lightTheme

darkTheme

Example semantic tokens (you may expand as needed):

appBackground

surface

surfaceSecondary

textPrimary

textSecondary

icon

border

shadow

overlay

gridLine

selectedCell

conflictCell

Update components to reference these tokens instead of hardcoded colors.

3) Background handling in Dark Mode

Because the app uses bright and dynamic backgrounds:

Keep existing backgrounds unchanged.

In Dark Mode, add a full-screen dark overlay layer above the background:

Black overlay with ~45–60% opacity

Optional subtle vertical gradient

This overlay ensures readability without redesigning each background.

4) Sudoku board behavior (VERY IMPORTANT)

Dark Mode must NOT invert the Sudoku board.

Board rules:

The Sudoku grid remains light for readability.

Do NOT use a black grid or white numbers.

In Dark Mode only:

Change the grid background from pure white to a slightly warmer off-white
Example:

Light mode: #FFFFFF

Dark mode board: #EFECE6 (warm, low-glare white)

Grid lines, numbers, and logic visuals remain unchanged.

Colored numbers (purple, teal, gold, diamond) stay exactly the same.

This ensures long-session comfort and avoids visual fatigue.

5) Numbers & skills visuals

Number colors remain unchanged in both themes.

Reveal yellow background and Scan red highlights must remain clearly visible on the warm board.

Do not recolor or invert skill effects.

6) UI elements affected by Dark Mode

Dark Mode applies to:

App background

Store screens

Diamonds shop

Settings modal

Cards, panels, headers, footers

Buttons and icons

The Sudoku grid itself stays light as described above.

7) Web / PWA details (nice to have)

Update the <meta name="theme-color"> dynamically based on the active theme.

Ensure safe-area spacing and full-screen layout remain correct.

**Designing Dark Mode**

I'm currently focused on the initial implementation of the Dark Mode feature. Right now, I'm fleshing out the 'Appearance' setting within the app's settings UI, including options for System, Light, and Dark modes. I'm prioritizing persistent storage for this setting, probably leveraging the existing `Storage` mechanism. Following this, I'll dive into crafting a modular, token-based theme system using CSS to handle the visual changes.


**Developing Theme Tokens**

I've been refining my approach to theme tokens. I've decided to create CSS variables for semantic tokens. Thinking about it, since I'm using Tailwind classes currently like `bg-stone-50`, I'll replace these with new semantic classes or CSS variables, with the dark theme controlled by adding a `.dark` class to the `<html>` or `<body>`. I'm starting with tokens like `appBackground`, `surface`, `textPrimary`, etc.


**Integrating System Preference**

I'm now integrating the system preference into the dark mode logic. I've updated `types.ts` and `utils/storage.ts` to accommodate the new appearance options ('system', 'light', 'dark'). I'm currently working on applying the `.dark` class to `document.documentElement` dynamically based on the stored setting and the user's system preference. My focus is on ensuring a smooth transition and implementing the background overlay for dark mode within `App.tsx`.


**Applying Theme to UI**

I'm now applying the dark theme to the UI elements. I've switched over Tailwind's utility classes to the CSS variables. For instance, I'm now setting `bg-[var(--app-background)]` in place of `bg-stone-50` and `text-[var(--text-primary)]` instead of `text-stone-800`. I'm starting by modifying the Sudoku game and its controls to align with the dark theme's palette, paying close attention to board background colors.


**Adjusting Theme Colors**

I'm now integrating the specific color values into the theming system. I've defined CSS variables for several colors, including `text-primary`, `surface-secondary`, and `border`, aligning them with the dark mode aesthetic. I'm focusing on consistency in the UI and ensuring seamless transitions when switching modes. Currently, I'm refactoring the `tailwind.config` file to utilize these variables, streamlining the implementation of the dark theme.


**Defining Tailwind Colors**

I'm now integrating the CSS variables into Tailwind's configuration, so the classes will be clearer. I'm focusing on defining a theme color set in `tailwind.config.js` named `t`, which will reference the CSS variables. This will help with the transition. Following this, I'll update the React components to use `bg-t-bg`, `text-t-primary`, etc. I will add a special note about the Sudoku board; I need to ensure it's not inverted in dark mode, and that it has a warm white background in both. I will name it `board-bg`.


**Implementing Screens**

I'm now applying the new semantic classes to all screens. I've updated the Splash, Difficulty, Levels, Store, and DiamondShop screens, replacing Tailwind utility classes with my semantic ones. Next, I'm integrating the background overlay with its correct z-index in `App.tsx` for visual depth and smooth transitions. I'm focusing on ensuring responsiveness and correct positioning across various screen sizes.


**Handling System Changes**

I've realized I need to add a listener to `window.matchMedia` for system changes. This is critical for real-time updates based on user preferences. Currently, I'm integrating this event listener within `App.tsx` and ensuring the dark mode class is updated accordingly. This is important to allow real-time changes to the dark mode, especially when toggling in a supported operating system. I'm making sure that I'm also updating the meta tag for the theme color, so the browser understands the appropriate theme, for browser tabs and context switches.


**Refactoring UI Components**

I'm now refactoring the `SudokuGame.tsx` file for a cohesive dark mode experience. The header's text color is now using the `text-t-secondary` variable. I've also updated the board's container background to `bg-t-board`, and addressed the cells' background to match, ensuring they are transparent or correctly styled in all modes. Lastly, the UI controls (buttons and number inputs) now use `bg-t-surface`, and I'm adding icons to `Icons.tsx` for visual confirmation of the dark/light mode toggle.


**Applying The Final UI Touches**

I'm now focusing on the final UI adjustments and ensuring complete dark mode integration. I've added 'Moon', 'Sun', and 'Laptop' icons to `Icons.tsx` and now I'm creating the 'Appearance' section in the `SettingsModal` within `App.tsx`. I'm verifying the Sudoku board colors, making sure the off-white background and grid lines are correct in dark mode. Next, I'll update the logic for the default settings and types, followed by implementing CSS variables and updating the Tailwind configuration in `index.html`. Finally, I'll address `App.tsx` logic and UI classes and add the overlay for the finishing touches.


**Completing Dark Mode**

I'm wrapping up the final touches for dark mode. I'm updating `SudokuGame.tsx`, updating the UI classes, and board logic. I've integrated `Moon`, `Sun`, and `Laptop` icons from `lucide-react`. I'm also preparing migration logic in `utils/storage.ts` to ensure existing users default to the 'system' appearance. Lastly, I'm defining the necessary CSS variables for both light and dark modes in `index.html` to finalize the theming system. I'm now making adjustments in `App.tsx` replacing hardcoded values to the theme's semantic classes.


**Defining Default Settings**

I'm now focusing on defining the default settings and types for the dark mode. I'm updating the `types.ts` file to include the new appearance options and setting the default appearance to 'system'. I'm also preparing the migration logic in `utils/storage.ts` to ensure existing users default to 'system' in a graceful way. Next, I'll update the logic for the "Appearance" section in the `SettingsModal` within `App.tsx` and adding logic to store the setting.

To implement the Dark Mode feature with a token-based theme system and the specific requirements for the Sudoku board, I will make changes to the following files:

1.  **`types.ts`**: Update `AppSettings` to include the `appearance` preference.
2.  **`utils/storage.ts`**: Set the default appearance to `system` and handle data migration.
3.  **`components/ui/Icons.tsx`**: Add `Sun`, `Moon`, and `Laptop` icons for the settings UI.
4.  **`index.html`**: Define the CSS variables for the theme tokens (`light` and `dark` modes) and update the Tailwind configuration to map these variables to utility classes (e.g., `bg-t-bg`, `text-t-primary`).
5.  **`App.tsx`**:
    *   Implement the theme detection logic (System/Light/Dark).
    *   Add the "Appearance" toggle to the Settings Modal.
    *   Add the dark mode overlay for backgrounds.
    *   Refactor the entire UI (Menu, Store, Levels, etc.) to use the new semantic theme tokens instead of hardcoded colors.
6.  **`components/SudokuGame.tsx`**:
    *   Update the game UI to use theme tokens.
    *   Implement the specific board coloring rule (Warm Off-White in Dark Mode, keeping grid lines and numbers high-contrast).

    *   This darkening effect is only applied during gameplay, keeping the menu screens cleaner and lighter as requested, while providing better contrast for the game board.

1) General rules

Each difficulty has levels 1–100 available by default.

Levels 101–200 exist but are completely hidden until unlocked.

The next 100 levels can ONLY be unlocked after completing 100/100 levels in that same difficulty.

2) Locked card UI (before 100%)

At the very bottom of each difficulty screen (after the list of levels 1–100), show ONE large locked card.

Locked card appearance:

Shows only:

A large lock icon

The progress percentage (example: 60%)

No title

No subtitle

No buttons

Greyed out / disabled

Not clickable

The purpose is to create tension and curiosity.

3) Progress animation (IMPORTANT)

When the user scrolls down and the locked card enters the viewport (meaning the user can see it):

Start an animation that:

Fills a progress bar from 0% → current progress %

Animates the % number counting up at the same time (0 → current)

Trigger this animation only when the card becomes visible

Use IntersectionObserver

Do NOT replay constantly on tiny scrolls

Either play once per screen session

Or replay only if the card fully leaves and re-enters view

4) When the player reaches 100%

When the player completes 100/100 levels in a difficulty:

UI change:

The lock icon disappears

The card becomes clickable

The card now shows:

A simple unlock line with the price, for example:

Unlock next 100 levels — 1200💎

Keep the design minimal (no extra text)

Super Easy → 700💎

Easy → 900💎

Normal → 1200💎

Hard → 1500💎

Intense → 1800💎

Impossible → 2200💎

When the card is clickable (100%) and the user taps it:

If the user has enough diamonds:

Subtract the required diamonds

Persist that Pack 2 is unlocked for that difficulty

Instantly reveal levels 101–200 (append them below)

Remove the unlock card OR replace it with a subtle “Unlocked” state

If the user does NOT have enough diamonds:

Show a simple message: “Not enough diamonds”

Show a button: “Get more 💎”

This opens the Diamonds shop

7) Persistence

Persist the following per difficulty:

Progress (0–200)

Whether Pack 2 is unlocked

Closing/reopening the app must keep:

Unlock state

Progress

Hidden/revealed levels

Do NOT show levels 101–200 in any form before unlock

Do NOT show text explaining the lock (keep it minimal)

The card itself is the explanation

### Important App Characteristics

Here are the key technical and design characteristics of your Sudoku app:

*   **Difficulty Scaling**: The difficulty is procedurally generated on the client side by removing a specific number of cells (holes) from a full grid.
    *   **Super Easy**: 32 holes (~49 clues)
    *   **Easy**: 38 holes (~43 clues)
    *   **Normal**: 48 holes (~33 clues)
    *   **Hard**: 54 holes (~27 clues)
    *   **Intense**: 57 holes (~24 clues)
    *   **Impossible**: 60 holes (~21 clues)

*   **Generation Logic**: It uses a seeded random number generator (based on Difficulty + Level ID) so that Level 1 is always the same for every user. It ensures the puzzle has exactly **one unique solution** by checking for ambiguity every time a number is removed.

*   **Progression System**:
    *   **Points**: Earned by completing levels; used to buy cosmetics and unlock skills.
    *   **Level Packs**: Levels 1-100 are free. Levels 101-200 and 201-300 are unlocked via point-purchasable packs.
    *   **Skills**: Auto-fill (Single), Scan (Board check), and Reveal (Random cell) are unlockable abilities.

*   **Tech Stack**: Built with **React 19**, styled with **Tailwind CSS**, and uses **LocalStorage** for persistence. It is designed as a PWA (Progressive Web App) with mobile-first touch targets.
